column3: The Hebrew says blessing Israel was “good in the eyes of the LORD”; BSB says it “pleased the LORD.”
The Hebrew says Balaam “lifted his eyes”; BSB says he “looked up.”
The Hebrew has singular “the eye”; BSB uses plural “eyes.”
The Hebrew says “falling” with “uncovered eyes”; BSB says “bows down” with eyes “wide open.”

The Hebrew gives devouring, dealing with bones, and crushing as finite verbs; BSB expresses these as purposes with “to devour,” “crush,” and “to pierce.”
The Hebrew asks who will rouse the lion without an explicit daring verb; BSB adds “dares.”
The Hebrew repeats Balak’s name as the speaker; BSB uses “he.”
The Hebrew says to flee to “your place” and repeats the honor root for the promised honor and its withholding; BSB specifies “your home” and uses the more specific “richly reward” and “reward.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the images “the mouth of the LORD” and “from my heart”; BSB says “the command of the LORD” and “of my own accord.”
The Hebrew says Balaam will “counsel” Balak about what will happen “at the end of the days”; BSB says “warn” him about “the days to come.”
The Hebrew leaves the oracle speaker unnamed and uses singular “the eye”; BSB supplies Balaam’s name and plural “eyes.”
The Hebrew repeats the knowledge root and says “falling” with “uncovered eyes”; BSB says “has knowledge” and “bows down” with eyes “wide open.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “a possession” and uses plural “his enemies”; BSB carries the possession through “as will Seir” and uses singular “his enemy.”
The Hebrew uses singular “a survivor” and says “from a city”; BSB uses plural “the survivors of the city.”
The Hebrew leaves the observer unnamed; BSB supplies “Balaam.”
The Hebrew names singular collective “the Kenite”; BSB uses plural “the Kenites.”
The Hebrew includes the question “until when?” before Asshur’s taking captive; BSB combines the clauses with “when.”
The Hebrew leaves the oracle speaker unnamed, without an explicit “Once more”; BSB supplies Balaam’s name and that introductory phrase.
The Hebrew repeats the afflicting verb for Asshur and Eber and ends with singular “he also”; BSB gives “subdue” once for both and ends with plural “they too.”
The Hebrew gives separate going and returning verbs and says “his place”; BSB combines these as “returned to his homeland.”
